issues.issue: Whether the IAD's decision is reviewed on correctness or reasonableness (whether a jurisdictional question arose)
issues.applicant_position: Appellant: the IAD's jurisdiction question is jurisdictional, so the Federal Court should have applied correctness.
issues.result_quote: the applicable standard of review of the IAD decision is reasonableness

issues.issue: Whether the IAD unreasonably held that subsection 63(2) requires a valid PR visa when the removal order is issued
issues.applicant_position: Appellant: a visa valid at arrival or at the s. 44 report suffices; IAD misread Ismail and should have applied McLeod.
issues.respondent_position: Not stated; IAD and Federal Court held the visa must be valid when the removal order is issued.
issues.result_quote: I disagree largely for the reasons given by the Federal Court, before which the appellant advanced these same arguments.

issues.issue: Whether the IAD failed to carry out a textual, contextual and purposive analysis of subsection 63(2)
issues.applicant_position: Appellant: the IAD had to undertake its own textual, contextual and purposive analysis.
issues.result_quote: it was reasonable for the IAD not to undertake its own statutory interpretation analysis
